name: Souks & Artisan Quarter
hero_subtitle: Thuya wood, silver jewellery and spice alleys — the craft heart of Essaouira’s medina.

overview.title: Workshops inside the walls
overview.p1: Essaouira’s souks mix everyday shopping with craft workshops. Thuya wood carving and silver work are local signatures; spices, argan products and textiles fill the narrower alleys.
overview.p2: Morning is quieter and better for watching artisans. Bargain politely where expected, keep bags closed, and step aside for carts in tight lanes.
overview.p3: Use the craft streets as a link between the Skala, the Mellah and a café stop — not only as a shopping list.

q1.question: What is Essaouira known for?
q1.answer: Thuya wood objects and silver jewellery are classic local crafts.

q2.question: Best time to shop?
q2.answer: Morning for calmer workshops and clearer light.

q3.question: Can I watch artisans work?
q3.answer: Often yes — ask before entering a workshop or taking photos.

q4.question: Fixed prices?
q4.answer: Some items are flexible; polite bargaining is common in many stalls.

q5.question: Shipping?
q5.answer: Larger workshops may arrange shipping — confirm costs in writing.
